claims.text_en: Sathon is one of Bangkok's 50 khets, 9.326 km2 south of the CBD, with three khwaeng: Thung Wat Don (3.195 km2, 34,618 people), Yan Nawa (2.090, 18,132) and Thung Maha Mek (4.041, 18,556) - 71,306 registered residents in Dec 2023. Boundaries (Thai Wikipedia): north - Bang Rak/Pathum Wan along Khlong Sathon and the south side of Rama IV; east - Khlong Toei/Yan Nawa along the Mae Nam railway line, Soi Chuea Phloeng 4 and Yen Akat road; south - Yan Nawa/Bang Kho Laem along Nang Linchi, Chan Kao, Khlong Chong Nonsi, Chan and Sathupradit roads to Khlong Khuay; west - the river midline (Khlong San across). The khet was created 9 November 1989 from Yan Nawa (branch office from 9 March 1989); the spelling สาธร was officially corrected in April 1999.

question_answers.question: identity/scope
question_answers.answer: Khet Sathon, 9.326 km2, three khwaeng (Thung Wat Don, Yan Nawa, Thung Maha Mek), bounded by Khlong Sathon + Rama IV south side (N), the Mae Nam railway/Yen Akat (E), Nang Linchi/Chan/Khlong Chong Nonsi/Sathupradit (S), river midline (W); created 9 Nov 1989 from Yan Nawa. In-polygon anchors: Saint Louis Hospital, MR Kukrit's House, Suan Phlu market, Wat Yannawa, 80 Phansa park, Taksin bridge park, canal-park segments, Wat Don cemetery, BRT Sathon stop. Out: the three BTS nodes (Surasak/Chong Nonsi/Saint Louis, in the road median), Sathorn Unique tower, Suan Pa Chaloem Phra Kiat tip, MRT Lumphini.

question_answers.question: everyday experience
question_answers.answer: CBD-south office khet with a residential interior: weekday Sathorn-corridor suits and embassy traffic, canal-park and royal-park weekends, quiet Yen Akat/Chan sois with heritage houses inland; the mall-and-BTS strip belongs to the excluded boundary. Subarea claims marked partial.

question_answers.question: values+mechanisms
question_answers.answer: Transport 7 = edge-loaded rail (three BTS nodes on the excluded corridor, MRT Lumphini just off the NE corner) plus the BRT Narathiwas corridor and Tha Sathorn boat - the interior is a km+ from any rail gate. DE 9 / food 9 = office-crowd market/cafe density (1,098 food POIs) + Suan Phlu/Wat Yannawa anchors. Green 9 = named-park access (80 Phansa 3.02 ha, canal park, Taksin bridge park) rather than in-khet acreage. Rent 5 = deepest stock (8,231 listings) and highest prices of the four khets.

question_answers.question: counter-evidence
question_answers.answer: Three: (1) green 9 cannot be reproduced from mapped in-khet green (~5-6 ha PIP-IN vs app 25.0 ha) - the score rides on named-park access, not acreage; (2) transport 7 is internally consistent only because the polygon excludes the BTS corridor the khet is famous for; (3) the canal park's water quality remains visibly poor ('slower than anticipated', odor complaints), tempering the green story.

question_answers.question: rhythm
question_answers.answer: Office mornings and lunch pulses on the corridor; embassy/school rhythms inland; the canal park and royal park (05:00-21:00) carry morning runners and evening aerobics; weekends move to parks and the riverside; nightlife concentrates on the north corridor around Chong Nonsi.

question_answers.question: walkability
question_answers.answer: Flat interior grid; the canal-park walkways and the royal-park loop give genuine walking infrastructure; Sathorn Rd itself is a hostile, congested crossing; no walking durations were derived from catchment radius in this bundle.

question_answers.question: daily life
question_answers.answer: Daily needs: Suan Phlu and neighbourhood wet markets, office-tower retail, Saint Louis Hospital + schools for the family layer, 12+ embassies for paperwork; leisure: 80 Phansa park, canal park, Wat Yannawa riverside, MR Kukrit's House museum.

question_answers.question: affordability vs stated figures
question_answers.answer: App 25,000/55,000 sits below HipFlat's portal means (1-bed USD 889 ~ 30k THB; 2-bed USD 1,730 ~ 59-60k) because the portal set skews Silom-edge and riverfront; the inland mid-market band (Nang Linchi/Yen Akat) is what pulls the blend down. Rent 5 = priciest of the four khets; prices gently falling (-5.8% vs Jan 2026).

question_answers.question: green/quiet with polygon honesty
question_answers.answer: Green: named parks are real and inside (80 Phansa renovated 2025-26, canal-park segments, Taksin bridge park, cemetery green) but the 25.0-ha app figure needs a counting rule; the 2.63-ha forest park at the west tip is polygon-OUT. Quiet: genuine in the interior sois; the corridor and Narathiwas BRT carry the noise. The excluded Sathorn corridor means 'Sathon address' and 'polygon interior' diverge for offices and nightlife.

question_answers.question: conditional fit
question_answers.answer: Strong fit: office-district professionals who want walk-to-work plus real parks (renovated royal park, canal park) and can pay CBD-south rents. Weak fit: budget renters (priciest of the four) and anyone whose daily life depends on being AT a BTS gate - the gates are on the excluded corridor, a km+ from the interior.

question_answers.question: recent changes 2024-2026
question_answers.answer: 80 Phansa royal park renovation (2025-2026); canal-park Phase 3 built out along Chan Road through 2025 (end-2025 target, unconfirmed); Blue & Green Network program active into 2026; rents drifting down; no rail changes inside the khet.

question_answers.question: uncertainties/outside-the-score
question_answers.answer: Unresolved: the 25.0-ha park counting rule (OSM ~5-6 ha in-polygon); whether Phase 3 of the canal park actually completed end-2025 (target only); BRT service details (no ridership/fare data body-read); khet membership of individual corridor towers; rent data single-family (PropertyScout 404). Safety 7 untested by any located statistic.

preview.text_en: The CBD's south annex: embassy rows, office towers and a renovated royal park along a canal being turned into Bangkok's first linear water-garden - at the batch's highest rents, with the BTS gates sitting on the boundary line the map excludes.

guide_lead.text_en: Sathon wraps three khwaeng of residential sois around the Sathorn office corridor, with the deepest rental stock of the batch (8,231 listings), 12+ embassies, Saint Louis Hospital, and the batch's best named-park access - the 80 Phansa royal park reopened in 2025-2026 with expanded green, and the 4.5 km Chong Nonsi canal park keeps extending even as its water quality lags. The honest asterisks: the BTS stations that give the district its name sit in the road median the app polygon excludes (transport 7, not 9), the 25-ha green figure needs a counting rule, and rents - though slipping - remain the priciest of the four researched khets.

strengths.text: Parks you can actually use: the renovated 80 Phansa royal park (05:00-21:00, lit loop, playground, stage) plus the canal-park walkway segments and Taksin bridge park - the batch's strongest named-green access.
Office-district completeness: Saint Louis Hospital and schools, 1,098 food POIs, wet markets inland, and a BRT corridor threading Narathiwas - daily life rarely requires leaving the khet.

tradeoffs.text: The transit paradox: three BTS stations carry the district's name but stand in the median the polygon excludes, leaving interior sois (Yen Akat, Chan, Nang Linchi) a kilometre-plus from any rail gate - hence transport 7.
Priciest of the batch: portal 1-bed averages ~USD 889 (~30k THB) with the blend at 25,000/55,000, and the canal park's water is still visibly poor despite the 2024-2026 build-out.

day_night.text: Weekdays pulse with office and embassy traffic on the corridor; the parks take over at dawn and dusk (05:00-21:00, lit for runners); weekends belong to the canal park and riverside; nightlife concentrates on the excluded north edge around Chong Nonsi while the interior goes quiet.

within_area_variation.text: Three Sathons: the excluded-but-famous Sathorn Rd corridor (towers, BTS, embassies' front doors), the residential Thung Wat Don/Yen Akat interior with heritage houses, and the canal-and-river east where the parks and Wat Yannawa sit - administratively one khet, split by the polygon.

conditional_fit.text: Choose it if you work in the CBD and want a walkable green routine (royal park loop, canal walkways) and full services at 25-30k for a 1-bed - and don't mind the BTS being a boundary feature rather than a door-step one.
Skip it if rent is the constraint (cheapest 1-beds here cost what Thon Buri charges for two) or if you need rail at the door in the interior sois.

uncertainties.text: Unresolved: the 25.0-ha park counting rule (OSM in-polygon ~5-6 ha); canal-park Phase 3 completion (target end-2025, unconfirmed); BRT service details; per-tower khet membership on the corridor; single-family rent data (PropertyScout 404). Anchors verified against OSM with no mismatch beyond the known corridor exclusions.

open_issues: park_ha 25.0 (3.5%) vs OSM in-polygon named green ~5-6 ha: gap plausibly = Wat Don cemetery, canal linear strips, road planting, institutional grounds; needs an app-methodology decision.

Sathorn Rd corridor exclusion: BTS median nodes + north-side offices + Sathorn Unique tower are polygon-OUT while being the khet's most-cited features; Thai Wikipedia lists Sathorn Unique as a khet landmark. Coordinator polygon audit recommended.
Transport 7 mechanism is our synthesis (edge-loaded rail + interior distance); no ridership/frequency data body-read.
Canal-park Phase 3 completion (end-2025 target, Deputy Gov Wisanu) and the ~472M THB budget are search-aggregated, not body-read; Nation (Jul 2026) confirms water-quality lag only.
Rent: single family (HipFlat) after PropertyScout 404; portal area bleeds into Silom/Saladaeng and Charoen Krung riverfront.
Safety 7: no district statistics in EN or TH; untested, not contradicted.
